summary: This Dockerfile builds a Go application in two stages to create a tiny, efficient container. First, it compiles the Go code into a standalone binary with no external dependencies, then it copies just that binary into an almost-empty container, resulting in a final image that's just a few megabytes instead of hundreds.

explanations.3: This pulls the official Go 1.22 image based on Alpine Linux (a tiny Linux distribution) and labels it 'builder' so we can reference it later.
explanations.9: CGO_ENABLED=0 disables C bindings so the binary has zero external dependencies; GOOS=linux ensures it runs on Linux; the -ldflags strip debug symbols to make the binary smaller; -o server names the compiled output file.
explanations.11: This starts a new stage with 'scratch', which is literally an empty container—just enough to run a binary with no OS or libraries.
explanations.13: This copies the compiled 'server' binary from the first stage (builder) into the final empty container so it has something to run.
